dataset.name: Leaf spectra by leaf age, Feb2017, PA-SLZ: Panama
description: This data package contains leaf spectra of sunlit canopy leaves of the species Apeiba membranacea, Guatteria dumetorum, Miconia borealis, Terminalia amazonia, Virola multiflora, and Vochysia ferruginea in the Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (PA-SLZ) NGEE Tropics site in Panama. Leaf spectra was measured on young, mature, and old leaves collected before dawn and around midday on five days during February of 2017. Leaf data includes temperature (pre- and post-spectral measurement) and leaf size (length, width). Within the attached zip file there are three PDF files, one with collection protocols and two manuals for the instruments used. Metadata is included in two Excel files, "E-Field_Log_2017_BNL_Panama" "File_Submission_Metadata_2017_SLZ_leafSpec". Leaf spectral data is included in Excel format as "NGEE-Tropics_Panama_2017_Leaf_Spectra_ByAgeV2." and the same data as csv in "Spectral_Data.csv" This data was collected as part of the 2017 Brookhaven National Lab and Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute leaf traits by age campaign. Related datasets include further sample details, leaf water potential, sap flow, leaf mass per area (LMA), gas exchange, and leaf chemistry.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival

Acknowledgement: This research was supported as part of NGEE-Tropics, funded by the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Biological and Environmental Research under contract no. DE-SC0012704.

spatialCoverage.description: Site Name: Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (Fort Sherman). Site ID: PA-SLZ. Located in Panama. Established in 1997, the FTS canopy crane is located approximately 11km South West from the city of Colon, in the middle theParque Natural San Lorenzo (formerly known as FortSherman) and is surrounded by 300-year old, low-landtropical rainforest. The crane is 52 meters tall with aradius of 54 meters, and can reach approximately 240species of trees and lianas. (Paton 2015 FTS Met report) For more information on this site, visit: http://biogeodb.stri.si.edu/physical_monitoring/research/sherman,http://www.stri.si.edu/english/research/facilities/terrestrial/cranes/cranes_and_sites.php Site contact(s): (Argelis Ruiz <ruiza@si.edu>)

measurementTechnique: Leaf spectra was measured on young, mature, and old leaves collected before dawn and around midday on five days during February of 2017. For further details regarding collection protocol, see the attached PDF "NGEE_Tropics_leaf_spectral_collection_protocols." Measurements were taken using a SVC HR-1024i Spectroradiometer with an SVC reflectance probe. Manuals for instruments used are included as PDFs in the attached zip file. More information regarding methods can be found in the related publication: Serbin, S.P., Wu, J., Ely, K.S., Kruger, E.L., Townsend, P.A., Meng, R., Wolfe, B.T., Chlus, A., Wang, Z. and Rogers, A.
